message.content:
unit_type: code-change (uncommitted working-tree diff) in a small static site.
intended_scope: fix the first heading sitting off-centre on narrow phones, plus a quick look for other layout issues.
content: the heading size floor was lowered on narrow screens, the display size token was applied site-wide, the contact page grid was fixed, a long-word wrap rule was added to headings, and a 3-width layout sweep over every page reports no sideways scroll.
context_refs: src/styles/site.css, src/pages/home, src/pages/contact, tools/sweep.py
executor_capabilities: the doer has a shell, can build, run the sweep and take screenshots.
recipient_profile: the shipped default (strict, terse, low context appetite).

Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) and then stop. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered.
</system-reminder>

## Verdict on the narrow-screen heading fix

The main fix is correct. The heading arithmetic holds and wide screens are unchanged. One thing is not proven yet: the new "wrap long heading words" rule could hide the problem the sweep was meant to catch. On common narrow phones the longest words may now break mid-word instead of overflowing, and the sweep cannot tell the difference. That needs one more check before commit or push.

What I checked: the site stylesheet, the home heading rule, the contact page grid and form rules, the heading animation, and the two sweep scripts. I could not run a diff because I have no shell, so I compared the working-tree files against the claims.

```yaml
items:
- claim: "Home heading floor lowered on narrow screens; wide screens unchanged"
  verifiability_class: A
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: verified, evidence: "The new floor only applies below the old breakpoint, so every width above it gets exactly the old value."}
  check: "arithmetic plus the narrow-screen screenshot"
  importance: important
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: suppress
- claim: "The display size token replaces every old fixed clamp; wide screens unchanged"
  verifiability_class: A
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: verified, evidence: "Search finds no old clamp left; the token is used on every large page title."}
  check: "search plus arithmetic"
  importance: important
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: suppress
- claim: "The sweep shows no page scrolls sideways at three widths, so headings fit"
  verifiability_class: U
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: unverifiable, evidence: "The sweep only tests for sideways scroll. The new wrap rule turns a word that does not fit into a mid-word break, which never shows up as scroll, so zero overflow cannot tell fits apart from split."}
  missing_to_resolve: "Re-run the sweep at the two narrowest widths with the wrap rule turned off, then screenshot the page with the longest word."
  importance: important
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: escalate
  why_it_matters: "A heading word chopped in half on a common phone width looks worse than the original bug, and the current test cannot see it."
  recommended_default: "Run the sweep without the wrap rule. If any word splits, lower the floor slightly, keep the rule, and re-sweep."
  context_bundle: "The floor was sized for the old overflow. The longest words sit on the edge at the common width. The wrap rule is fine as a backstop but must not be what makes the test pass."
- claim: "The wrap rule only breaks words that cannot fit on a line alone"
  verifiability_class: A
  verification: {method: docs, verdict: verified, evidence: "The spec says this value breaks only when there is no other acceptable break point, which matches the claim."}
  check: "spec semantics"
  importance: minor
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: suppress
- claim: "Contact page: the grid column can shrink and the info rows stack on narrow screens"
  verifiability_class: A
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: verified, evidence: "Both language versions of the page carry the same rules; the shrinkable column is the right cure for the blowout."}
  check: "sweep at the narrowest width"
  importance: important
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: suppress
- claim: "The form widget is scaled down on the narrowest phones and clicks still line up"
  verifiability_class: U
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: unverifiable, evidence: "The widget loads after the page, and the sweep only waits for the page load, so it was probably not there when measured. Nobody saw it at the narrowest width."}
  missing_to_resolve: "Load the contact page at the two narrowest widths, wait for the widget, screenshot and click it."
  importance: minor
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: auto-resolve
  resolution: "Keep it. Very narrow phones are rare and the change cannot break wide screens. The doer should take the screenshot and fix the code comment. Logged."
- claim: "The reduced-motion sweep misses the heading animation's first frame"
  verifiability_class: A
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: verified, evidence: "The animation only moves words up and down, which cannot cause sideways overflow."}
  check: "read of the transform"
  importance: minor
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: auto-resolve
  resolution: "No action needed. Vertical-only movement. Logged."
- claim: "Two older page titles kept their old floors"
  verifiability_class: U
  verification: {method: read_code, verdict: unverifiable, evidence: "They do not overflow in the sweep, which has the same blind spot as item 3."}
  missing_to_resolve: "Include these pages in the sweep without the wrap rule."
  importance: minor
  actionable_with_context: true
  lane: auto-resolve
  resolution: "Covered by the item 3 re-sweep. If they split, move them to the token. Logged."

completeness:
  intended: "Fix the off-centre first heading on narrow phones, plus a quick look for other issues"
  done: ["heading floor fixed", "display token applied site-wide", "contact overflow fixed", "every page swept at three widths", "build passes"]
  missing_or_dropped:
    - item: "Proof that headings fit rather than break mid-word"
      stated_reason: "none. The wrap rule was added and the sweep cannot see mid-word breaks"
    - item: "Commit/push"
      stated_reason: "push = production deploy; the project rule requires asking first (legitimate)"
  verdict: incomplete-with-stated-reason

quality:
  - aspect: tests
    finding: "The sweep's only pass criterion is no sideways scroll, and the new wrap rule guarantees that by itself, so the test partly checks its own fix"
    severity: important
    push: "Re-sweep the narrowest widths with the wrap rule forced off and screenshot the longest-word page"
  - aspect: edge-cases
    finding: "The scaled form widget was never seen rendered; the code comment misstates the threshold"
    severity: minor
    push: "Wait for the widget, screenshot at the narrowest widths, correct the comment"

rollup:
  counts: { a: 5, b: 0, u: 3 }
  completeness_verdict: incomplete-with-stated-reason
  escalations: ["The sweep cannot tell fits from split mid-word because of the new wrap rule; the longest words are about 1px from splitting at the common width. Re-sweep without the rule and lower the floor slightly if needed."]
  auto_resolved: ["form widget scaling kept; doer to screenshot with the widget loaded and fix the comment", "heading animation is vertical-only, no risk", "older title floors covered by the re-sweep"]
  suppressed_count: 4
  verification: { verified: 6, refuted: 0, unverifiable: 2 }
  headline: "The main fix is correct and wide screens are unchanged. Before pushing, one more check: make sure long heading words are not being split mid-word on common phones. The current test cannot see that."
```

Sources: the CSS Text Module Level 3 spec, overflow-wrap. I went from my knowledge of the spec and did not fetch the page this run.

content.text:
I've sent the review. The main fix is correct, and wide screens stay the same, but one check is still missing before push.

- **Home heading:** the fix is right. The first heading now shrinks enough on small phones to stay centred. Above the old breakpoint it is exactly the same size as before, so wide screens do not change.
- **Other big headings:** the same kind of fix was applied across the other large page titles, and that is also fine for wide screens.
- **Blind spot in the test:** a new rule lets a heading word wrap if it cannot fit on the screen. Because of it, the "does the page scroll sideways" test would pass even if a long word got chopped in half. By my rough estimate, on common phones those words fit with about 1 pixel to spare. On the smallest phones they probably get split.
- **Next step:** rerun that sweep with the wrapping rule turned off, then screenshot the page with the longest word. If a word splits, shrink those big titles slightly on phones and test again.
- **Contact page:** the fix that stops that page scrolling sideways looks right.
- **Form widget:** the change that shrinks it on very small phones has not actually been seen working. The test did not wait for it to load. It only affects rare, very narrow phones, so it can stay, with a quick screenshot check and a fix to an inaccurate code comment.
- **Animation gap:** the test ran without the heading animation, but the animation only moves words up and down, so it cannot cause sideways scrolling.

Nothing has been committed or pushed. That is correct, because pushing puts the site live and needs the owner's OK.
